newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana-Pacific to close plywood plants.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana-Pacific to close plywood plants.

text.p: Louisiana-Pacific Corp said on Tuesday it would temporarily close six of its seven plywood plants on Monday, February 3.
The closure -- which is expected to last two weeks -- is necessary because of log shortages brought about by unusually rainy weather in east Texas and Louisiana, the company said.
Louisiana-Pacific operates plywood plants in Urania and Logansport, La.; and in five Texas locations: New Waverly, Cleveland, Lufkin, Bon Wier and Jasper. The Jasper plant will remain open.
"We're hopeful that the weather will cooperate and we will be able to build up our plywood log inventories by mid-February," said Rick Frost, vice president of timber and procurement.
Louisiana-Pacific has sufficient inventory to meet the needs of its contract plywood customers with no interruption, the company said in a statement.
